summary.title: Professional summary
summary.paragraph1: My main focus is backend engineering and building institutional systems. I work with Laravel/PHP, Node.js/TypeScript, and Java/Spring Boot, using PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, and other technologies depending on each solution's requirements.
summary.paragraph2: I build REST APIs, system integrations, authentication, access control, auditing, queues, and asynchronous processing. I also work on frontend applications with Vue.js and React when a project calls for full-stack work.
summary.paragraph2b: I work with publishing and deployment configurations for Cloudflare, Vercel, and Fly.io, Docker containers, and GitHub Actions CI/CD (including AWS S3 and CloudFront deployments in collaboration), plus remote access via SSH, FTP/SFTP, and WordPress.
summary.paragraph3: My experience includes academic systems, research platforms, editorial solutions, automations, and institutional applications built for UniEVANGÉLICA, Fábrica de Tecnologias Turing, and the Brazilian Air Force. I have a growing interest in software architecture, cloud, observability, security, and applied AI for business systems.

aila.title: Aila — Smart Peer Reviewer Recommendation
aila.problem: Finding qualified reviewers who match a manuscript's topic is slow, manual work for a journal's editorial team.
aila.impact: Supports reviewer selection: classifies the manuscript by CNPq area with local AI and ranks reviewers discovered via OpenAlex and ORCID across four tiers, with a traceable justification. The final decision stays with the editorial team.
aila.roleShort: I authored all 72 repository commits: a Python/FastAPI backend, local AI with a cloud fallback, reviewer ranking, invitation records and RBAC, plus the Vue 3 frontend.
aila.result: Explainable reviewer ranking, 6 ADRs, an operations runbook and 112 passing tests; 70 PostgreSQL-dependent tests were skipped in the recorded run.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: A platform supporting the scientific editorial process, using academic data and review history to help identify reviewers who match a given manuscript.

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: Thematic classification of manuscripts by local AI (Ollama, with a cloud fallback), reviewer qualification in four tiers from OpenAlex and ORCID, ranking with a traceable justification, and invitation records per manuscript. Richer invitation history and recurrence analysis are on the roadmap.

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: Python/FastAPI backend on PostgreSQL, with local AI via Ollama (cloud fallback) for thematic classification, semantic embeddings for ranking, and a Vue 3 (Vite) frontend. Argon2 authentication and RBAC, decisions recorded in 6 ADRs, and Docker deployment.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: Author of all 72 repository commits: reviewer domain modeling, ranking, local-AI integration, invitation records, authentication, and tests.

tabs.title: Results
content: Explainable ranking, 6 ADRs and an operations runbook. In the recorded run, 112 tests passed and 70 PostgreSQL-dependent tests were skipped.

esports.title: E-Sports UniEVANGÉLICA Portal — 5th edition
esports.problem: A recurring institutional e-sports tournament needed per-modality registration and a public history of past editions.
esports.impact: Per-modality registration and tournament management with separate editions: the 5th edition on the home page and the 4th preserved on a historical route.
esports.roleShort: I built, with another developer, the backend (NestJS, Sequelize, PostgreSQL) and the frontend (Nuxt 4): per-modality registration, editions, and API security.
esports.result: 5th edition published, 4th preserved as history, and three P0 security issues fixed on 12 Aug 2026.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: An institutional e-sports tournament with multiple editions over time, requiring per-modality registration, edition-specific rules, and a public history of past editions.

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: Separate editions (theme, schedule, and rules per edition) let the 5th edition take over the home page while keeping the 4th accessible as history, with per-modality registration and an admin area.

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: NestJS 11 backend with Sequelize and PostgreSQL 16, JWT session in an HttpOnly cookie persisted in the database, per-route rate limiting, and helmet. Nuxt 4 frontend with Nuxt UI and Tailwind 4.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: Author of 80% of the backend commits (37 of 46) and 77% of the frontend (65 of 84), with another developer on the rest: editions, per-modality registration, and security fixes.

tabs.title: Results
content: 5th edition published, 4th edition on a historical route, and three P0 fixes: JWT_SECRET required in production, session bound to the JWT user, and wildcard CORS blocked with credentials.

jac.title: JAC – Academic and Community Journey
jac.problem: The project explores how to bring event schedules and registration together and record attendance verifiably, with access tailored to each role.
jac.impact: Platform with a public event catalog, registration, QR-code wallet, points and workspaces for participants, staff, coordinators and exhibitors. Current check-in uses QR codes; browser geolocation is disabled in this version.
jac.roleShort: I implemented parts of the backend and frontend, registration and attendance flows, session-based authentication with CSRF protection, and targeted fixes from a security audit.
jac.result: In the test run recorded on 2026-10-23, 353 unit tests passed (182 backend, 171 frontend); 10 PostgreSQL-dependent tests were skipped. Concurrency was validated locally. Production readiness and cutover remain pending.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: JAC explores a platform for discovering academic events, reviewing schedules, registering and recording attendance, with role-specific rules and history.

tabs.title: Implemented flows
tabs.content: Public event catalog and status, registration, QR-code wallet, attendance, points, administration and exhibitor lead capture. Geolocation is disabled in this version; current attendance uses QR codes.

tabs.title: Architecture
tabs.content: Node.js/Express 5, Prisma and PostgreSQL backend; Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia and Vue Router frontend. The React base remains in the production history; promotion of the new interface depends on a cutover that has not been approved.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: I implemented backend and frontend features, registration and attendance flows, session-based authentication and CSRF protection. I fixed specific audit findings, including duplicate points and a CSRF configuration issue.

tabs.title: Security and privacy
tabs.content: The project documents a security audit with six findings; SEC-001 and SEC-004 were addressed. Consent for exhibitor lead sharing is explicit and revocable. The status of remaining findings and institutional policies must be confirmed before making any compliance claim.

tabs.title: Tests and status
content: In the run recorded on 2026-10-23, 353 unit tests passed: 182 backend and 171 frontend; 10 PostgreSQL-dependent tests were skipped. Concurrency was validated locally. This does not count E2E tests as passing or confirm the current deployment.
Production readiness remains pending: the API, active Worker configuration, staging and cutover need validation. The repositories are private and are not linked publicly from this case.

lionFanstone.title: James Fanstone System Rewrite
lionFanstone.problem: An institutional academic-research system built in Laravel needed to move to a more sustainable foundation without interrupting the system already in production.
lionFanstone.impact: Backend rewrite of an institutional academic-research platform, migrating from the legacy Laravel system to Java and Spring Boot, now in production.
lionFanstone.roleShort: I built (83 of 83 commits) the Java 21 and Spring Boot 4 backend: architecture, domain, Flyway migrations, SOAP integration with CNPq/Lattes, and decisions recorded in ADRs.
lionFanstone.result: In production, with 31 controllers, 26 Flyway migrations, 482 automated tests and CI.

tabs.title: Context
tabs.content: UniEVANGÉLICA's institutional academic-research system (where I contributed specific features, like enrollment and notice reports, on the legacy Laravel system) needed to move to a more sustainable foundation, migrating the research domain to a new architecture.

tabs.title: Impact
tabs.content: Incremental backend rewrite in Java and Spring Boot: users and profiles with multi-profile login, permissions, auditing, academic output (Qualis/CAPES and JCR), projects with drafts, attachments and approval, work plans with scoring, and Lattes resume import through a SOAP integration with CNPq.

tabs.title: Stack
tabs.content: Java 21, Spring Boot 4, PostgreSQL with Flyway (26 versioned migrations), Spring Security via session and cookie with RBAC, ArchUnit for architecture rules, Swagger, and CI on GitHub Actions. Actuator restricted to health and info after an audit finding.

tabs.title: My role
tabs.content: Author of every commit in the repository (83 of 83): architecture, domain modeling, migrations, SOAP integration with CNPq/Lattes, and ADRs that guide the incremental migration from the legacy system.

tabs.title: Results
content: 31 REST controllers, 26 Flyway migrations and 482 tests passed in the recorded suite, in production. The split between unit and integration files has not been rechecked.
